chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Aban, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who owned a slave who had wealth, and the slave asked his master for mukatabah (contract of manumission), is it permissible for the master to stipulate that he does not contract with him except at a high price? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَة: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: Can a master refuse to free his slave by demanding a high price in the mukatabah contract?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the master's discretionary right to set the mukatabah price, specifically validating the stipulation of 'ghala'' (a high or substantial sum) as a legitimate condition. This ruling underscores the contractual flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing masters to balance financial compensation with the slave's potential ability to pay, thereby facilitating manumission while protecting the owner's rights.
